Layer B writes the merged PI snapshot to a new {{oe_payments_contract.OXSTRIPESNAPSHOT}} JSON column with a Stripe-side digest as the idempotency token, invalidated hard by the existing webhook handlers and softly by a 5-minute TTL; warm renders then pay zero Stripe cost. The audit-log table ({{oe_payments_transaction}}) stays read-only audit; nothing in this report touches its writer contract.

column1: Define Allowed Special Characters for Account / Billing & Shipping Address Fields
column29:
*Description*
Review and enforce input validation rules for account creation and billing/shipping address fields. Current validation should be updated to use field-specific allowlists (preferred) instead of inconsistent character handling.

*Validation Rules by Field*

h3. 1. First Name / Last Name

*Allow:*

* Unicode letters (including accents/diacritics)
* Spaces
* Apostrophe ({{'}})
* Hyphen ({{-}})
* Optional period ({{.}})

*Block:*

* {{: ; < > { } [ ] ( ) | \ / \}} ~ ! @ # $ % ^ * = + " ? , & _`

----

h3. 2. Additional Info

*Allow:*

* Letters, numbers, spaces
* {{' - . , / #}}

*Block:*

* {{< > { } [ ] | \}} ~ ! @ $ % ^ * = +`

----

h3. 3. Street

*Allow:*

* Letters, numbers, spaces
* {{' - . , /}}

*Block:*

* {{: ; < > { } [ ] | \}} ~ ! @ $ % ^ * = +`

----

h3. 4. House Number (No.)

*Allow:*

* Numbers
* Letters
* {{- /}}

----

h3. 5. Postal Code

*Allow:*

* Letters
* Numbers
* Spaces
* {{-}}

----

h3. 6. City

*Allow:*

* Unicode letters
* Spaces
* {{' - .}}

*Block:*

* {{: ; < > { } [ ] ( ) | \ / \}} ~ ! @ # $ % ^ * = + " ? , & _`

----

h3. 7. Company

*Allow:*

* Letters, numbers, spaces
* {{' - . & ,}}

*Block:*

* {{< > { } [ ] | \}} ~ ! @ $ % ^ * = +`

----

h3. 8. VAT ID

*Allow:*

* Letters
* Numbers
* {{-}}
* Spaces (if country format requires it)

----

h3. 9. Phone / Cell / Personal Phone / Telefax

*Allow:*

* Numbers
* Spaces
* {{+ - ( )}}

----

h2. Also Reject Across All Fields

*Tabs* ({{\t}})
Invisible spacing characters created when users paste values from spreadsheets, documents, or external systems. Can cause hidden formatting issues and failed matches in downstream systems.

*Newlines* ({{\n}}, {{\r}})
Line breaks should not be accepted in single-line inputs. They can break form formatting, exports, integrations, and may introduce parsing issues.

*Null bytes* ({{\0}})
Non-printable control character with no valid user input purpose. Historically linked to truncation bugs, parser issues, and security edge cases.

*Zero-width / invisible Unicode characters*
Examples: zero-width space, zero-width joiner, zero-width non-joiner. These are not visible to users, but can make two values look identical while actually being different (very problematic for search, deduplication, fraud checks, and validation).

*Other control characters*
Non-printing characters (ASCII control range and similar Unicode controls) that can interfere with storage, logs, exports, integrations, or system behavior. These have no valid use in name or address fields.

----

*Acceptance Criteria*

* Validation is enforced consistently on create and edit flows
* Existing valid names like O'Connor and Anne-Marie are accepted
* Colon ({{:}}) is rejected in name fields
* Validation uses allowlist logic where possible
* Field-level error messages are user friendly

02/Apr/26 5:09 PM;63da45808978d7a435392127;h1. oad Tests — Stripe Payment (k6 Browser)

Load testing framework for the Stripe payment module using [k6|https://k6.io/] with the browser module (Chromium). Tests replicate Playwright e2e flows under concurrent load.

h2. Quick Start

{noformat}# 1. Copy env config
cp .env.dist .env
# Edit .env with your shop URL and credentials

# 2. Dry-run (1 VU, 1 iteration — validate selectors work)
./bin/run.sh --scenario happy_path

# 3. Baseline (10 VU/min, 2 min)
./bin/run.sh --baseline

# 4. Full load (100 VU/min, 10 min)
./bin/run.sh --full
{noformat}

!http://localhost:63342/markdownPreview/572014390/commandRunner/runrun.png|width=250!

k6 is auto-installed on first run if not found in PATH.

h2. Configuration

h3. {{.env}} file

{noformat}K6_BASE_URL=https://daniil.oxiddev.de   # Shop URL
K6_TEST_USER_PASSWORD=useruser           # Test user password
K6_BROWSER_ENABLED=true                  # Required: enables k6 browser module
K6_BROWSER_HEADLESS=true                 # false = show browser window
{noformat}

!http://localhost:63342/markdownPreview/572014390/commandRunner/runrun.png|width=250!

{quote}*Important:* Custom vars use {{LOAD_}} prefix (not {{K6_}}). k6 reserves {{K6_DURATION}}, {{K6_VUS}} etc. as built-in overrides that conflict with our scenario config.{quote}

h3. CLI Options

||Flag||Description||Default||
|{{--dry-run}}|1 VU, 1 iteration per scenario|(default)|
|{{--baseline}}|10 VU/min, 2 min| |
|{{--full}}|100 VU/min, 10 min| |
|{{--endurance}}|100 VU/min, 30 min| |
|{{--scenario NAME}}|Run single scenario|{{all}}|
|{{--vus N}}|Custom VU/min (disables dry-run)|100|
|{{--duration N}}|Custom steady-state minutes|10|
|{{--ramp-up N}}|Custom ramp-up minutes|2|
|{{--headed}}|Show browser (not headless)|headless|
|{{--help}}|Show usage| |

h3. Examples

{noformat}# Single scenario debug with visible browser
./bin/run.sh --headed --scenario happy_path

# Custom: 50 VU/min for 5 minutes, cancellation only
./bin/run.sh --vus 50 --duration 5 --scenario cancellation

# Override shop URL
K6_BASE_URL=https://other-shop.dev ./bin/run.sh --baseline
{noformat}

!http://localhost:63342/markdownPreview/572014390/commandRunner/runrun.png|width=250!

h2. Scenarios

||Scenario||Traffic||Description||Playwright Source||
|{{happy_path}}|40%|Login -> cart -> Stripe -> pay -> thank you|{{Checkout.spec.ts}}|
|{{cancellation}}|20%|Login -> cart -> Stripe -> back (abandon)|{{coupon-survives-back-navigation.spec.ts}}|
|{{guest_coupon}}|15%|Guest -> cart -> coupon -> user step|{{GuestOrders.spec.ts}}, {{CouponsDiscounts.spec.ts}}|
|{{payment_failure}}|15%|Login -> cart -> declined card -> retry -> success|{{PaymentEdgeCases.spec.ts}}|
|{{threeds}}|10%|Login -> cart -> 3DS card -> challenge -> thank you|{{Checkout.spec.ts}} (3DS)|

h2. Project Structure

{noformat}tests/load/
├── .env                     # Local config (gitignored)
├── .env.dist                # Template
├── k6.config.js             # Entry point: scenario builder + thresholds
├── bin/
│   ├── run.sh               # CLI runner script
│   └── k6                   # Auto-installed k6 binary (gitignored)
├── helpers/
│   ├── config.js            # Env vars + test data (cards, coupons)
│   ├── metrics.js           # Custom k6 Rate/Counter/Trend
│   ├── auth.js              # Login, cookies, language
│   ├── shop.js              # Products, cart, checkout, coupons
│   └── stripe.js            # Card fill, pay, 3DS, thank you
├── scenarios/
│   ├── happy-path.js        # Full checkout flow
│   ├── cancellation.js      # Abandon at Stripe
│   ├── guest-coupon.js      # Guest + coupon
│   ├── payment-failure.js   # Declined -> retry
│   └── threeds.js           # 3DS authentication
└── results/                 # Run output logs (gitignored)
{noformat}

h2. Architecture

h3. k6 Browser Module

k6's browser module runs Chromium — same engine as Playwright. Helpers use the same CSS selectors as the Playwright e2e suite but with k6's locator API.

*Key difference from Playwright:* k6 locators don't support {{.first()}}, {{{ hasText }}} option, {{getByRole()}}, or {{frameLocator()}}. Use {{:has-text()}} pseudo-selectors and {{page.frames()}} instead.

h3. Selector Mapping

Helpers mirror Playwright's {{Helper.ts}} methods:

||k6 Helper||Playwright Helper||
|{{loginAndSetup()}}|{{setupLoggedInSession()}}|
|{{addProductsToCart()}}|{{goToAxlePartsFromMenu()}} + {{addFirstTwoProductsToCartFromList()}}|
|{{navigateToCheckout()}}|{{startCheckoutViaMiniBasket()}}|
|{{selectStripeAndOrder()}}|{{selectDigitalWalletPayment()}} + {{clickNext()}} + {{clickOrderNow()}}|
|{{fillStripeCard()}}|{{fillStripeCardDetailsWithCard()}}|
|{{clickStripePay()}}|{{clickPayOnStripeCheckout()}}|
|{{handle3DS()}}|{{click3DSButton()}}|
|{{verifyThankYou()}}|{{assertThankYouPageAndGetOrderNumber()}}|

h3. Test Data

Hardcoded from {{tests/e2e/playwright/playwright/fixtures/stripe-test-cards.ts}}:

* *Cards:* 4242424242424242 (success), 4000000000000002 (declined), 4000000000003220 (3DS)

h3. Thresholds

||Metric||Threshold||Description||
|{{browser_http_req_failed}}|< 5%|HTTP error rate|

|{{contract_state_valid}}|= 100%|Valid contract transitions|
|{{stripe_api_errors}}|< 10|Stripe errors|
|{{checkout_duration}} p95|< 60s|Full browser flow time|

07/Apr/26 6:30 PM;63da45808978d7a435392127;h1. Load Tests — Stripe Payment (k6 Browser)

Load testing framework for the Stripe payment module using [k6|https://k6.io/] with the browser module (Chromium). Tests replicate Playwright e2e flows under concurrent load.

h2. Quick Start

{noformat}# Dry-run — 1 VU, 1 iteration (validate the flow works)
K6_BROWSER_ENABLED=true \
K6_BASE_URL=http://localhost.local \
K6_TEST_USER_EMAIL=playwright.user@oxid-esales.dev \
K6_BROWSER_ARGS='ignore-certificate-errors' \
LOAD_DRY_RUN=true \
LOAD_SCENARIO=happy_path \
./bin/k6 run k6.config.js
{noformat}

!http://localhost:63342/markdownPreview/523931552/commandRunner/runrun.png|width=250!

h2. Running Tests

All commands run from {{tests/load/}}. The k6 binary is at {{./bin/k6}}.

h3. Environment Variables

||Variable||Description||Default||
|{{K6_BROWSER_ENABLED}}|*Required.* Enables k6 browser module|—|
|{{K6_BASE_URL}}|Shop URL (HTTP, no trailing slash)|{{https://daniil.oxiddev.de}}|
|{{K6_TEST_USER_EMAIL}}|Login email for authenticated scenarios|random {{loadtest_user_NNN}}|
|{{K6_TEST_USER_PASSWORD}}|Login password|{{useruser}}|
|{{K6_BROWSER_ARGS}}|Chromium flags (comma-separated)|—|
|{{LOAD_DRY_RUN}}|{{true}} = 1 VU, 1 iteration|{{false}}|
|{{LOAD_SCENARIO}}|Run single scenario by name|{{all}}|
|{{LOAD_TARGET_VUS}}|Target virtual users per minute|{{100}}|
|{{LOAD_DURATION}}|Steady-state duration in minutes|{{10}}|
|{{LOAD_RAMP_UP}}|Ramp-up duration in minutes|{{2}}|

{quote}*Note:* Use {{LOAD_}} prefix for custom vars. k6 reserves {{K6_VUS}}, {{K6_DURATION}} etc. as built-in overrides that conflict with our scenario config.{quote}

h3. Examples

{noformat}# --- Base command (always needed) ---
export K6_BROWSER_ENABLED=true
export K6_BASE_URL=http://localhost.local
export K6_TEST_USER_EMAIL=playwright.user@oxid-esales.dev
export K6_BROWSER_ARGS='ignore-certificate-errors'

# 1. Dry-run single scenario (debug / validate selectors)
LOAD_DRY_RUN=true LOAD_SCENARIO=happy_path ./bin/k6 run k6.config.js

# 2. Smoke test — 5 VUs/min, 2 min, happy_path only
LOAD_TARGET_VUS=5 LOAD_DURATION=2 LOAD_SCENARIO=happy_path ./bin/k6 run k6.config.js

# 3. Baseline — 10 VUs/min, 5 min, all scenarios
LOAD_TARGET_VUS=10 LOAD_DURATION=5 ./bin/k6 run k6.config.js

# 4. Medium load — 50 VUs/min, 10 min
LOAD_TARGET_VUS=50 LOAD_DURATION=10 ./bin/k6 run k6.config.js

# 5. Full load — 100 VUs/min, 10 min (default)
./bin/k6 run k6.config.js

# 6. Endurance — 100 VUs/min, 30 min
LOAD_DURATION=30 ./bin/k6 run k6.config.js

# 7. Stress test — 200 VUs/min, 10 min
LOAD_TARGET_VUS=200 ./bin/k6 run k6.config.js

# 8. Single scenario under load
LOAD_TARGET_VUS=20 LOAD_DURATION=5 LOAD_SCENARIO=cancellation ./bin/k6 run k6.config.js

# 9. Custom ramp-up (slow start)
LOAD_TARGET_VUS=50 LOAD_RAMP_UP=5 LOAD_DURATION=10 ./bin/k6 run k6.config.js
{noformat}

!http://localhost:63342/markdownPreview/523931552/commandRunner/runrun.png|width=250!

h3. Load Profile

When {{LOAD_DRY_RUN}} is not set, k6 uses a *ramping-arrival-rate* executor:

{noformat}VUs/min
  ^
  |          ┌──────────────────────────┐
  |         /│      steady state        │\
  |        / │    (LOAD_DURATION min)   │ \
  |       /  │                          │  \
  |      /   │                          │   \
  |     /    │                          │    \
  |    /     │                          │     \
  |───/──────┴──────────────────────────┴──────\───> time
  | ramp-up                              cool-down
  | (LOAD_RAMP_UP min)                   (1 min)
{noformat}

Traffic is split across scenarios according to the distribution in {{helpers/config.js}}:

||Scenario||Share||At 100 VUs/min||
|{{happy_path}}|40%|40 VUs/min|
|{{cancellation}}|20%|20 VUs/min|
|{{guest_coupon}}|15%|15 VUs/min|
|{{payment_failure}}|15%|15 VUs/min|
|{{threeds}}|10%|10 VUs/min|

h2. Scenarios

||Scenario||Description||
|{{happy_path}}|Login → add to cart → checkout → Stripe Checkout → pay with 4242 card → thank you page|
|{{cancellation}}|Login → add to cart → checkout → Stripe Checkout → navigate back without paying|
|{{guest_coupon}}|Guest → add to cart → apply coupon → navigate to checkout user step|
|{{payment_failure}}|Login → add to cart → checkout → pay with declined card → see error → retry with valid card|

h2. k6 Browser API Notes

k6 browser is *not* Playwright. Key differences that affect helper code:

* No {{.first()}} on locators — k6 locator already targets first match
* No {{page.waitForURL()}} — poll {{page.url()}} in a loop

These critical/high issues from other modules do *not* exist in our codebase:

||Issue (from other module)||Our Status||Evidence||
|*HMAC bypass* (Adyen: default true, injection)|NOT VULNERABLE|Uses Stripe SDK {{Webhook::constructEvent()}} — fail-closed|
|*SQL injection* (AmazonPay: direct concat)|NOT VULNERABLE|All queries use prepared statements or QueryBuilder|
|*IDOR* (old Stripe: StripeFinishPayment, Unzer: deletePayment)|NOT VULNERABLE|No order/user loads by ID from request without ownership check|
|*SSRF* (Unzer: Apple Pay merchantValidationUrl)|NOT VULNERABLE|No server-side HTTP calls with user-controlled URLs|
|*Unauthenticated state-change endpoint* (AmazonPay: poll)|NOT VULNERABLE|All state-changing endpoints require session/signature|
|*Session hijacking via setVariable('usr')* (old Stripe)|NOT VULNERABLE|No code sets user session variable from request/order data|
|*unserialize() without allowed_classes* (PayPal, easyCredit)|NOT VULNERABLE|No {{unserialize()}} calls in entire module|
|*DOM-XSS via innerHTML / jQuery .html()* (Unzer: 6 templates, old Stripe)|NOT VULNERABLE|No {{innerHTML}} or {{.html()}} in active JS/templates|
|*Open redirect from API response* (AmazonPay)|NOT VULNERABLE|All redirects hardcoded or config-based|
|*Session-ID/stoken in redirect URLs to provider* (old Stripe)|NOT VULNERABLE|Uses contract tokens instead (HMAC-signed, one-time)|
|*Missing CSRF on state-changing endpoints* (Adyen, AmazonPay, easyCredit, Unzer)|NOT VULNERABLE|All endpoints validate {{checkSessionChallenge()}}|
|*No webhook endpoint* (easyCredit)|NOT VULNERABLE|Full webhook implementation with guard chain|
|*Weak crypto for tokens* (PayPal: md5+mt_rand, AmazonPay: uuid fallback)|NOT VULNERABLE|Uses {{hash_hmac('sha256')}} + {{hash_equals()}}|
|*Timing attack on secret comparison* (old Stripe: {{==}})|NOT VULNERABLE|Uses {{hash_equals()}} for all token comparisons|
|*Floating-point amount comparison* (old Stripe)|NOT VULNERABLE|Uses integer cents throughout ({{(int) round($x * 100)}})|
|*getRawValue() on user data* (old Stripe, easyCredit)|NOT VULNERABLE|No {{getRawValue()}} usage on user/API data|

h1. Idempotency Implementation Analysis Report

*Date:* 2026-02-05 *Sprint:* Analysis Sprint 41 *Status:* 🔍 ANALYSIS COMPLETE

----

h2. Executive Summary

The idempotency implementation has *a critical gap* between documentation and actual implementation:

||Component||Documented Purpose||Implementation Status||
|{{oe_payments_idempotency}} table|Prevent duplicate API calls to payment providers|❌ *NOT USED* - Dead table|
|{{WebhookIdempotencyChecker}}|Prevent duplicate webhook processing|✅ *IMPLEMENTED* - Uses {{oe_payments_webhooklogs}}|

*Key Finding:* The {{oe_payments_idempotency}} table was created to prevent excessive API requests to payment providers, but *no code actually uses it*. The table is completely dead.

----

h2. 1. Original Plan (From Documentation)

h3. Purpose: Prevent Duplicate Charges

From {{docs/oe_payments_docs/legacy_dev_architecture/architecture/02-database-and-models.md}}:

{noformat}### Table 10: oe_payments_idempotency (CRITICAL)

**Purpose:** Prevent duplicate charges (P0 feature)
{noformat}

h3. Designed Schema

{noformat}CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS oe_payments_idempotency (
    OXID CHAR(32) NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    OXKEY VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL UNIQUE,       -- Idempotency key
    OXORDERID CHAR(32) NOT NULL,              -- FK to oxorder
    OXOPERATION VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL,         -- createPayment, capturePayment, refundPayment
    OXRESULT TEXT,                            -- Cached result (JSON)
    OXSTATUS VARCHAR(32),                     -- processing, completed, failed
    OXCREATED DATETIME NOT NULL,
    OXEXPIRES DATETIME NOT NULL,

    INDEX IDX_KEY (OXKEY),
    INDEX IDX_EXPIRES (OXEXPIRES),
    INDEX IDX_ORDER_OPERATION (OXORDERID, OXOPERATION)
);
{noformat}

h3. Intended Workflow (Never Implemented)

{noformat}1. Before API Call:
   - Generate idempotency key: md5(orderId + operation + timestamp)
   - Check if key exists in oe_payments_idempotency
   - If exists AND status='completed': return cached OXRESULT
   - If exists AND status='processing': wait/retry
   - If not exists: insert with status='processing'

2. Make API Call to Stripe/PayPal

3. After API Response:
   - Update oe_payments_idempotency with:
     - OXSTATUS = 'completed' or 'failed'
     - OXRESULT = JSON response from provider

4. Cleanup:
   - Cron job deletes expired entries (OXEXPIRES < NOW())
{noformat}

----

h2. 2. Actual Implementation (Current State)

h3. What Exists

h4. Database Table: ✅ Created (But Not Used)

The table IS created by migration:

* *File:* {{payment-component/migration/data/Version20251031140200.php}}
* *Lines 129-183:* Creates {{oe_payments_idempotency}} with all columns

{noformat}private function createPaymentIdempotencyTable(Schema $schema): void
{
    $tableName = 'oe_payments_idempotency';
    // ... creates table with OXKEY, OXORDERID, OXOPERATION, OXRESULT, OXSTATUS, etc.
}
{noformat}

h4. Test Verification: ✅ Table Exists

From {{tests/Integration/Database/MigrationStructureTest.php}}:

{noformat}$this->assertTrue(
    $this->tableExists('oe_payments_idempotency'),
    'Table oe_payments_idempotency should exist (from payment-component)'
);
{noformat}

h3. What Does NOT Exist

h4. ❌ No IdempotencyRepository

{noformat}# Search result: NO FILES FOUND
Grep for "IdempotencyRepository" - 0 results
{noformat}

!http://localhost:63342/markdownPreview/1830235665/commandRunner/runrun.png|width=250!

h4. ❌ No IdempotencyService

{noformat}# Search result: NO FILES FOUND
Grep for "IdempotencyService" - 0 results
{noformat}

!http://localhost:63342/markdownPreview/1830235665/commandRunner/runrun.png|width=250!

h4. ❌ No IdempotencyModel

{noformat}# Search result: NO FILES FOUND
Grep for "IdempotencyModel" - 0 results
{noformat}

!http://localhost:63342/markdownPreview/1830235665/commandRunner/runrun.png|width=250!

h4. ❌ No Code Writes to Table

!http://localhost:63342/markdownPreview/1830235665/commandRunner/runrun.png|width=250!

----

h2. 3. What IS Actually Implemented: WebhookIdempotencyChecker

h3. Implementation

*File:* {{payment-component/src/Webhook/WebhookIdempotencyChecker.php}}

{noformat}class WebhookIdempotencyChecker implements WebhookIdempotencyCheckerInterface
{
    private array $processedEvents = [];

    public function __construct(
        private readonly WebhookLogRepositoryInterface $logRepository
    ) {}

    public function isProcessed(string $eventId): bool
    {
        if (isset($this->processedEvents[$eventId])) {
            return true;
        }
        return $this->logRepository->existsByEventId($eventId);
    }

    public function markAsProcessed(string $eventId): void
    {
        $this->processedEvents[$eventId] = true;
        $log = new WebhookLog($eventId, new DateTimeImmutable(), 'processed');
        $this->logRepository->save($log);
    }
}
{noformat}

h3. Key Points

# *Uses Different Table:* {{oe_payments_webhooklogs}}, NOT {{oe_payments_idempotency}}
# *Different Purpose:* Prevents duplicate WEBHOOK processing, not API calls
# *Actually Works:* Used by {{WebhookProcessor.php}}

h3. Usage in WebhookProcessor

*File:* {{payment-component/src/Webhook/WebhookProcessor.php}}

{noformat}public function process(array $webhookData): void
{
    // ...
    if ($this->idempotencyChecker->isProcessed($eventId)) {
        $this->logger->info('Webhook already processed, skipping', ['eventId' => $eventId]);
        return null;
    }
    // ... process webhook ...
    $this->idempotencyChecker->markAsProcessed($eventId);
}
{noformat}

----

h2. 4. Gap Analysis

h3. Documented vs Implemented

||Feature||Documentation||Implementation||
|Webhook duplicate prevention|Mentioned in architecture|✅ *IMPLEMENTED* via WebhookIdempotencyChecker|
|API call duplicate prevention|"P0 feature", "CRITICAL"|❌ *NOT IMPLEMENTED*|
|oe_payments_idempotency table|Full schema documented|❌ *DEAD* - Created but unused|
|Cached API responses|OXRESULT column documented|❌ *NOT IMPLEMENTED*|
|Operation tracking|OXOPERATION (createPayment, capturePayment, refundPayment)|❌ *NOT IMPLEMENTED*|

h3. Root Cause

The architecture documentation (v4.0.0, October 2025) planned for two types of idempotency:

# *Webhook idempotency* - Implemented using {{oe_payments_webhooklogs}}
# *API call idempotency* - Never implemented, table created but abandoned

The work was partially done during Sprint 2 (Ticket 10: Database Layer) but only the migration was completed. The service layer for {{oe_payments_idempotency}} was never built.

----

h2. 5. Business Impact

h3. Current State

*Without API Idempotency Protection:*

* Double-click on "Capture Payment" button could potentially create duplicate captures
* Network timeout + retry could create duplicate charges
* Race conditions in webhook handlers could trigger duplicate API calls

*Mitigating Factors:*

# Stripe SDK has built-in idempotency keys (passed in header)
# Payment providers generally have their own duplicate prevention
# Contracts track capture/refund amounts, limiting double-processing

h3. Risk Assessment

||Risk||Likelihood||Impact||Mitigation||
|Duplicate capture|Low|Medium|Stripe SDK idempotency|
|Duplicate refund|Low|Medium|Contract amount tracking|
|Duplicate payment creation|Very Low|High|Contract state machine|

----

h2. 6. Recommendations

h3. Option A: Remove Dead Code (Recommended)

*Effort:* Low (1-2 hours) *Risk:* None

# ❌ Remove {{oe_payments_idempotency}} table from migrations
# ❌ Remove tests that verify the table exists
# ✅ Keep {{WebhookIdempotencyChecker}} (actually used)
# Update documentation to reflect actual state

h3. Option B: Implement API Idempotency

*Effort:* High (2-3 days) *Risk:* Medium (regression potential)

If the original plan is still needed:

# Create {{IdempotencyRepository}} interface and implementation
# Create {{IdempotencyService}} with:
#* {{getOrCreate(orderId, operation): IdempotencyKey}}
#* {{markCompleted(key, result)}}
#* {{markFailed(key)}}
# Wrap capture/refund operations with idempotency checks
# Add cron job for cleanup

h3. Option C: Rely on Provider SDKs

*Effort:* None *Risk:* Low

Most modern payment SDKs handle idempotency:

{noformat}// Stripe already supports this
$stripe->paymentIntents->capture($id, [], [
    'idempotency_key' => 'unique_key_here'
]);
{noformat}

*Recommendation:* Document that we rely on Stripe SDK idempotency features instead of implementing our own.

----

h2. 7. Conclusion

The {{oe_payments_idempotency}} table is *dead code*:

* Created by migration but never used
* No repository, service, or model implemented
* Documented as "P0 feature" but abandoned

The actual idempotency implementation uses {{WebhookIdempotencyChecker}} with the {{oe_payments_webhooklogs}} table for webhook duplicate prevention, which is working correctly.

*Recommended Action:* Sprint to remove dead {{oe_payments_idempotency}} table OR document that API idempotency is handled by Stripe SDK.

----

* {{payment-component/migration/data/Version20251031140200.php}} - Creates the unused table
* {{payment-component/src/Webhook/WebhookIdempotencyChecker.php}} - Actual implementation
* {{docs/oe_payments_docs/legacy_dev_architecture/architecture/02-database-and-models.md}} - Original plan
* {{docs/oe_payments_docs/dev_history_phase_0/DONE/SPRINT-2-TICKET-10-database-layer.md}} - Sprint that created table

h1. ACP/MCP Foundations for Agentic Commerce

*Date:* 2026-02-09 *Sprint:* 47 (prerequisite research) *Status:* Complete

----

h2. Executive Summary

Two complementary protocols enable AI agents to conduct commerce on behalf of humans:

* *MCP (Model Context Protocol)* — the intelligence layer: how agents discover tools, resources, and capabilities
* *ACP (Agentic Commerce Protocol)* — the transaction layer: how agents execute purchases securely

Together they form the foundation for *agentic commerce* — AI agents that research, negotiate, and complete purchases without human micro-management of each step.

This report covers the technical foundations of both protocols and analyzes how they map to the existing stripe module architecture.

----

h2. 1. Model Context Protocol (MCP)

h3. 1.1 Origins

Released by Anthropic in November 2024. Adopted by OpenAI in March 2025. Donated to the *Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)* under the Linux Foundation in December 2025, co-founded by Anthropic, Block, and OpenAI. Current spec version: {{2025-11-25}}.

h3. 1.2 Architecture

MCP is a *client-server protocol* built on JSON-RPC 2.0:

{noformat}┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              MCP Host (AI Application)              │
│  e.g., Claude Desktop, ChatGPT, custom agent        │
│                                                      │
│  ┌────────────┐  ┌────────────┐  ┌────────────┐    │
│  │ MCP Client │  │ MCP Client │  │ MCP Client │    │
│  └──────┬─────┘  └──────┬─────┘  └──────┬─────┘    │
└─────────┼───────────────┼───────────────┼───────────┘
          │               │               │
   ┌──────▼──────┐ ┌──────▼──────┐ ┌──────▼──────┐
   │ MCP Server  │ │ MCP Server  │ │ MCP Server  │
   │ (local)     │ │ (local)     │ │ (remote)    │
   │ Filesystem  │ │ Database    │ │ Stripe      │
   └─────────────┘ └─────────────┘ └─────────────┘
{noformat}

*Three participant types:*

||Role||Description||
|*Host*|AI application that coordinates MCP clients (Claude, ChatGPT, custom agent)|
|*Client*|Component within host maintaining a connection to one MCP server|
|*Server*|Program exposing tools, resources, and prompts to clients|

h3. 1.3 Transport Mechanisms

||Transport||Use Case||Auth||
|*STDIO*|Local process communication, no network overhead|N/A (process-level)|
|*Streamable HTTP*|Remote servers, HTTP POST + optional SSE streaming|OAuth, Bearer tokens, API keys|

h3. 1.4 Server Primitives

MCP servers expose three types of capabilities:

*Tools* — executable functions the AI can invoke:

{noformat}{
  "name": "create_checkout_session",
  "title": "Create Checkout Session",
  "description": "Create a Stripe Checkout Session for the given cart",
  "inputSchema": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "items": {
        "type": "array",
        "items": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "product_id": { "type": "string" },
            "quantity": { "type": "integer" }
          },
          "required": ["product_id", "quantity"]
        }
      },
      "currency": { "type": "string", "default": "EUR" }
    },
    "required": ["items"]
  }
}
{noformat}

*Resources* — data sources (product catalogs, order history, configuration).

*Prompts* — reusable templates for LLM interactions (checkout assistance, product recommendations).

h3. 1.5 Lifecycle

Stateful protocol with capability negotiation handshake:

# Client sends {{initialize}} with {{protocolVersion}}, {{capabilities}}, {{clientInfo}}
# Server responds with its {{protocolVersion}}, {{capabilities}}, {{serverInfo}}
# Client sends {{notifications/initialized}}
# Connection active — client can call {{tools/list}}, {{tools/call}}, {{resources/list}}, etc.

h3. 1.6 JSON-RPC Message Format

Three message types:

{noformat}// Request (expects response)
{ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "tools/call",
  "params": { "name": "create_checkout", "arguments": { "items": [...] } } }

// Response
{ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1,
  "result": { "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "Session created: cs_abc" }] } }

// Notification (no response, no id)
{ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": "notifications/tools/list_changed" }
{noformat}

h3. 1.7 PHP SDK

Official PHP SDK ({{mcp/sdk}}) maintained with The PHP Foundation. PHP 8.1+, PSR standards. *Status: experimental pre-v1.0.*

{noformat}// Attribute-based tool registration
#[McpTool]
public function createCheckout(array $items, string $currency = 'EUR'): array
{
    // ...
}

// Server builder
$server = Server::builder()
    ->setServerInfo('oxid-stripe-mcp', '1.0.0')
    ->setDiscovery(__DIR__, ['src'])
    ->build();
$server->run(new StdioTransport());
{noformat}

h3. 1.8 Stripe's Existing MCP Server

Stripe already provides an MCP server at {{https://mcp.stripe.com}} with 30+ tools covering customers, products, payments, subscriptions, invoices. Authentication via OAuth or restricted API keys.

----

h2. 2. Agentic Commerce Protocol (ACP)

h3. 2.1 Origins

Co-developed by *Stripe and OpenAI*. First release: September 29, 2025. Apache 2.0 license.

*Spec versions:*

||Version||Key Addition||
|{{2025-09-29}}|Initial release|
|{{2025-12-12}}|Fulfillment enhancements|
|{{2026-01-16}}|Capability negotiation|
|{{2026-01-30}}|Extensions, discounts, payment handlers|

h3. 2.2 Four Parties

{noformat}┌──────────┐     ┌──────────┐     ┌──────────────┐     ┌──────────────┐
│  Buyer   │────▶│ AI Agent │────▶│  Merchant    │────▶│  Payment     │
│ (Human)  │     │ (ChatGPT,│     │ (OXID Shop   │     │  Provider    │
│          │     │  Claude)  │     │  + Stripe)   │     │  (Stripe)    │
└──────────┘     └──────────┘     └──────────────┘     └──────────────┘
 Discovers        Interfaces       Merchant of          Processes
 products,        with buyer,      record: products,    payment via
 approves         executes         pricing, tax,        Shared Payment
 payment          checkout         fulfillment          Tokens
{noformat}

The *merchant remains merchant of record* — full control over products, pricing, transactions, and fulfillment.

h3. 2.3 Three Specifications

# *Product Feed Specification* — Catalog syndication to AI agents

* Formats: TSV (recommended), CSV, XML, JSON
* Required fields: {{id}}, {{title}}, {{description}}, {{price}}, {{currency}}, {{availability}}, {{image_url}}
* Refresh: up to every 15 minutes
* Security: HTTPS, Bearer token, IP whitelisting

# *Agentic Checkout Specification* — REST endpoints for checkout lifecycle

||Endpoint||Method||Purpose||
|{{/checkouts}}|POST|Create checkout session|
|{{/checkouts/:id}}|GET|Retrieve checkout|
|{{/checkouts/:id}}|PUT|Update checkout (shipping, options)|
|{{/checkouts/:id/complete}}|POST|Finalize payment|
|{{/checkouts/:id/cancel}}|POST|Cancel checkout|

*Checkout statuses:* {{not_ready_for_payment}} → {{ready_for_payment}} → {{completed}} (or {{canceled}})

# *Delegated Payment Specification* — Shared Payment Tokens (SPTs)

SPTs are Stripe's payment primitive for agentic commerce:

||Property||Description||
|Scoped|Bound to a specific seller ({{network_id}})|
|Time-bound|Expires at specified timestamp|
|Amount-limited|Maximum transaction amount|
|One-time use|Linked to specific checkout session|
|Revocable|Can be cancelled at any time|
|Observable|Webhook events for lifecycle tracking|

h3. 2.4 Checkout Create Request

{noformat}{
  "items": [
    { "id": "sku_123", "quantity": 2 }
  ],
  "buyer": {
    "first_name": "Jane",
    "last_name": "Doe",
    "email": "jane@example.com"
  },
  "fulfillment_address": {
    "name": "Jane Doe",
    "line_one": "123 Main St",
    "city": "San Francisco",
    "state": "CA",
    "country": "US",
    "postal_code": "94105"
  }
}
{noformat}

h3. 2.5 Checkout Complete Request

{noformat}{
  "payment_data": {
    "token": "spt_granted_abc123",
    "provider": "stripe",
    "billing_address": {
      "line_one": "123 Main St",
      "city": "San Francisco",
      "state": "CA",
      "country": "US",
      "postal_code": "94105"
    }
  }
}
{noformat}

h3. 2.6 Checkout Response Model

  "id": "cs_abc123",
  "status": "ready_for_payment",
  "currency": "eur",
  "line_items": [
    {
      "id": "li_1",
      "item": { "id": "sku_123", "quantity": 2 },
      "base_amount": 5000,
      "discount": 0,
      "subtotal": 5000,
      "tax": 950,
      "total": 5950
    }
  ],

    {

h3. 2.9 ACP Can Be Implemented as MCP Server

ACP endpoints can be exposed as MCP tools. This means a single MCP server can provide both data access (resources) and transactional capabilities (ACP checkout tools).

h3. 3.4 What Is New vs. What Exists

*Already exists (reuse):*

* Contract lifecycle (state machine, conditions, metadata)
* Event system (handlers, dispatcher, context)
* Checkout session creation (handler chain)
* Contract repository (CRUD, state queries)
* Idempotency (duplicate prevention)
* Webhook processing pipeline

*Must be built:*

* MCP server layer (PHP, Streamable HTTP transport)
* ACP checkout endpoint controllers (REST or MCP tools)
* SPT payment flow (Shared Payment Token confirmation)
* Product feed generation (catalog → ACP format)
* ACP-to-contract state mapping
* ACP response formatters (line items, totals, fulfillment options)
* Agent authentication/authorization

h2. 4. Security Considerations

h3. 4.1 Authentication

* MCP remote servers require OAuth or Bearer token auth
* ACP requires HTTPS with Bearer token + HMAC webhook signatures
* SPTs are scoped, time-limited, and one-time-use by design

h3. 4.2 Fraud Risks

* *78% of financial institutions* expect increased fraud from agentic commerce
* Attack vectors: AI-created fake storefronts, bot-initiated transactions, conversational social engineering
* Mitigation: Stripe Radar integration (already in module), SPT amount limits, agent identity verification

h3. 4.3 Authorization Model

* SPTs enforce: seller scope, amount limit, time expiry, single use
* Agent must be pre-authorized by buyer (consent flow)
* Module must validate SPT before creating PaymentIntent

11/Feb/26 5:04 PM;63da45808978d7a435392127;h1. Report: Testing ACP Checkout with Serverless LLMs

*Date:* 2026-02-12 *Context:* Sprint 47 (ACP + UCP + MCP Support) *Goal:* Enable human testers to validate the ACP checkout flow using a free/serverless LLM as a real AI agent — no local GPU, no paid API keys required.

----

h2. Problem Statement

Our ACP checkout exposes 6 MCP tools ({{list_products}}, {{create_checkout}}, {{get_checkout}}, {{update_checkout}}, {{submit_checkout}}, {{cancel_checkout}}). Unit and integration tests validate the PHP backend, but we need a way for a *human tester* to:

# Point a real LLM at our MCP server
# Give it a natural-language instruction ("buy a red t-shirt")
# Watch the LLM discover tools, call them in the right order, and complete checkout
# Verify the contract reaches {{COMMITTED}} / {{FULFILLED}} state

This requires a *tool-calling LLM* that can run serverlessly (no local GPU) and an *MCP client* that connects to our MCP endpoint.

----

h2. Approach Overview

{noformat}┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Human Tester's Machine (no GPU needed)                      │
│                                                               │
│  ┌─────────────────┐     ┌──────────────────────────────┐   │
│  │ Terminal / CLI    │     │ Serverless LLM (HuggingFace)  │   │
│  │ (tiny-agents)    │◄───►│ Qwen2.5-72B / Llama-3-70B     │   │
│  └────────┬────────┘     └──────────────────────────────┘   │
│           │ MCP JSON-RPC                                      │
│           ▼                                                   │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │ Our MCP Server (https://shop.example.com/stripemcp)       │ │
│  │ tools/list → 6 ACP tools                                  │ │
│  │ tools/call → create_checkout, submit_checkout, etc.       │ │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
{noformat}

Three practical options, ranked by ease of setup:

||#||Option||Setup Time||LLM Cost||Best For||
|1|*HuggingFace Tiny Agents* (recommended)|~5 min|Free tier|Quick validation, CI smoke tests|
|2|*MCP Inspector + manual tool calls*|~2 min|None|Debugging tool schemas, protocol verification|
|3|*Custom Python agent loop*|~15 min|Free tier|Custom scenarios, regression suites|

----

h2. Option 1: HuggingFace Tiny Agents (Recommended)

h3. What It Is

[Tiny Agents|https://huggingface.co/blog/tiny-agents] is a minimal MCP-powered agent built into the {{huggingface_hub}} Python package. It's ~70 lines of code internally — a while loop that alternates between LLM tool-calling and MCP tool execution until the task is complete.

h3. Prerequisites

{noformat}pip install "huggingface_hub[mcp]>=0.32.0"
{noformat}

!http://localhost:63342/markdownPreview/2005264916/commandRunner/runrun.png|width=250!

Free HuggingFace account + API token from [huggingface.co/settings/tokens|https://huggingface.co/settings/tokens].

h3. Setup

Create an agent config directory (e.g., {{tests/e2e/acp-agent/}}):

{{agent.json}}*:*

{noformat}{
    "model": "Qwen/Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct",
    "provider": "nebius",
    "servers": [
        {
            "type": "http",
            "url": "https://shop.example.com/stripemcp"
        }
    ]
}
{noformat}

{{PROMPT.md}} (system prompt for the agent):

{noformat}You are a shopping assistant testing an e-commerce checkout.

Your goal: complete a purchase using the available MCP tools.

Steps:
1. Call list_products to see what's available
2. Pick a product and call create_checkout with it
3. Call get_checkout to verify the session
4. Call submit_checkout to complete the purchase
5. Report the final checkout status

Always use the tools — never guess product IDs or prices.
{noformat}

h3. Running

{noformat}# Set your free HuggingFace token
export HF_TOKEN="hf_..."

# Run the agent
tiny-agents run ./tests/e2e/acp-agent/

# Then type your instruction:
# > "Buy the cheapest available product"
{noformat}

!http://localhost:63342/markdownPreview/2005264916/commandRunner/runrun.png|width=250!

The agent will:

# Connect to the MCP server at {{https://shop.example.com/stripemcp}}
# Call {{tools/list}} to discover the 6 ACP tools
# Use the LLM to decide which tools to call and in what order
# Stream results back to the terminal in real-time

h3. Supported Models (Free Tier)

||Model||Provider||Tool-Calling Quality||Notes||
|{{Qwen/Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct}}|nebius|Excellent|Recommended — best open-source tool caller|
|{{meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct}}|nebius/together|Good|Solid alternative|
|{{deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-0528}}|novita|Good|Reasoning model, may be verbose|
|{{mistralai/Mixtral-8x22B-Instruct-v0.1}}|together|Good|Fast, decent tool calling|

All available via HuggingFace Inference Providers free tier — no credit card required.

h3. Alternative: Run via Python Script

{noformat}import asyncio
from huggingface_hub.inference._mcp import Agent

async def main():
    agent = Agent(
        model="Qwen/Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct",
        provider="nebius",
        api_key="hf_...",
        servers=[{
            "type": "http",
            "url": "https://shop.example.com/stripemcp"
        }],
        prompt="You are a shopping assistant. Use the available tools to complete purchases."
    )

    await agent.load_tools()

    async for event in agent.run("Buy the cheapest available product"):
        if hasattr(event, 'content') and event.content:
            print(event.content, end="", flush=True)

asyncio.run(main())
{noformat}

----

h2. Option 2: MCP Inspector (Protocol Debugging)

h3. What It Is

[MCP Inspector|https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector] is Anthropic's official visual testing tool for MCP servers. It provides a web UI to call {{tools/list}}, {{tools/call}}, and inspect JSON-RPC messages — *no LLM needed*.

h3. When to Use

* Verify tool schemas are correct before connecting an LLM
* Debug individual tool calls with specific parameters
* Validate JSON-RPC request/response format
* Check auth (Bearer token) handling

h3. Setup

{noformat}# Use version >= 0.14.1 (CVE-2025-49596 patched)
npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector@latest
{noformat}

!http://localhost:63342/markdownPreview/2005264916/commandRunner/runrun.png|width=250!

Opens a web UI at {{http://localhost:6274}}. Configure:

* *Transport:* Streamable HTTP
* *URL:* {{https://shop.example.com/stripemcp}}
* *Headers:* {{Authorization: Bearer <agent-api-key>}}

h3. Usage

# Click *"List Tools"* — should show 6 ACP tools with JSON Schema parameters
# Click any tool (e.g., {{create_checkout}}) — fill in parameters, execute
# Inspect the raw JSON-RPC request and response
# Walk through the full checkout flow manually

h3. Limitation

MCP Inspector is for *protocol verification*, not agentic testing. The human decides which tools to call and in what order — there's no LLM reasoning.

----

h2. Option 3: Custom Python Agent Loop

h3. When to Use

* Need custom validation logic between tool calls
* Building a regression test suite
* Want to use a specific LLM provider (Groq, Together AI)

h3. Architecture

{noformat}import json
from openai import OpenAI

# Use HuggingFace Inference API (free tier, OpenAI-compatible)
client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://router.huggingface.co/v1",
    api_key="hf_..."  # Free HuggingFace token
)

# Or use Groq (free tier, very fast)
# client = OpenAI(
#     base_url="https://api.groq.com/openai/v1",
#     api_key="gsk_..."  # Free Groq API key
# )

MODEL = "Qwen/Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct"  # HuggingFace
# MODEL = "llama-3.3-70b-versatile"    # Groq
{noformat}

h3. MCP Client Setup

{noformat}from mcp import ClientSession
from mcp.client.streamable_http import streamablehttp_client

async def connect_to_mcp(server_url: str, bearer_token: str):
    """Connect to our MCP server and discover tools."""
    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {bearer_token}"}

    read, write, _ = await streamablehttp_client(server_url, headers=headers)

    async with ClientSession(read, write) as session:
        await session.initialize()

        # Discover tools
        tools_response = await session.list_tools()
        tools = tools_response.tools

        # Convert to OpenAI tool format
        openai_tools = []
        for tool in tools:
            openai_tools.append({
                "type": "function",
                "function": {
                    "name": tool.name,
                    "description": tool.description,
                    "parameters": tool.input_schema
                }
            })

        return session, openai_tools
{noformat}

h3. Agent Loop

{noformat}async def run_agent(user_instruction: str, server_url: str, token: str):
    """Run a complete agent loop: LLM ↔ MCP tools."""
    session, tools = await connect_to_mcp(server_url, token)

    messages = [
        {"role": "system", "content": "You are a shopping assistant. Use the tools to complete purchases."},
        {"role": "user", "content": user_instruction}
    ]

    max_turns = 10  # Safety limit
    for _ in range(max_turns):
        # 1. Ask LLM what to do
        response = client.chat.completions.create(
            model=MODEL,
            messages=messages,
            tools=tools,
            tool_choice="auto"
        )

        assistant_message = response.choices[0].message

        # 2. If no tool calls, we're done
        if not assistant_message.tool_calls:
            print(f"Agent: {assistant_message.content}")
            return assistant_message.content

        # 3. Execute each tool call via MCP
        messages.append(assistant_message)
        for tool_call in assistant_message.tool_calls:
            name = tool_call.function.name
            args = json.loads(tool_call.function.arguments)

            print(f"  → Calling {name}({json.dumps(args, indent=2)})")

            # Execute via MCP session
            result = await session.call_tool(name, args)

            print(f"  ← {result.content[:200]}...")

            messages.append({
                "role": "tool",
                "tool_call_id": tool_call.id,
                "name": name,
                "content": json.dumps(result.content)
            })

    print("Agent: Max turns reached")
{noformat}

h3. Running

{noformat}pip install openai "mcp[streamable-http]"

python acp_test_agent.py "Buy a red t-shirt, size M"
{noformat}

!http://localhost:63342/markdownPreview/2005264916/commandRunner/runrun.png|width=250!

----

h2. Free LLM Provider Comparison

||Provider||Free Tier||Tool-Calling Models||Speed||Setup||
|*HuggingFace Inference*|Monthly credits (generous)|Qwen2.5-72B, Llama-3.3-70B, DeepSeek-R1|Medium|{{pip install huggingface_hub}}|
|*Groq*|Free API key|Llama-3-Groq-70B-Tool-Use, Llama-3.3-70B|Very fast|{{pip install groq}}|
|*Together AI*|$25 startup credits|Llama-3.3-70B, Mixtral-8x22B|Fast|{{pip install together}}|

All three expose OpenAI-compatible APIs, so switching between them requires only changing {{base_url}} and {{api_key}}.

h3. HuggingFace Inference Providers (Primary Recommendation)

* *Free tier:* Monthly inference credits, no credit card
* *Pro tier:* $2/month for more credits + pay-as-you-go
* *API:* OpenAI-compatible ({{https://router.huggingface.co/v1}})
* *Key feature:* Built-in MCP support via Responses API — can make remote MCP calls natively
* *Models:* Routes to backend providers (Nebius, Together, Novita, etc.) automatically

h3. Groq (Best for Speed)

* *Free tier:* Free API key with rate limits
* *Specialty:* Ultra-fast inference (tokens/second leader)
* *Models:* {{llama-3-groq-70b-tool-use}} — specifically fine-tuned for tool calling (89% on BFCL benchmark)
* *API:* OpenAI-compatible ({{https://api.groq.com/openai/v1}})

----

h2. Recommended Testing Workflow

h3. For Quick Validation (Human Tester)

{noformat}1. Set up MCP Inspector          → Verify tools/list returns 6 tools correctly
2. Set up Tiny Agents            → Point at MCP server with Qwen2.5-72B
3. Give natural language prompts  → "Buy the cheapest product", "Add 2 red shirts to cart"
4. Observe tool call sequence     → Verify LLM calls tools in correct order
5. Check shop admin               → Verify contract/order created in OXID
{noformat}

h3. For Regression Testing (CI/Scripted)

{noformat}1. Custom Python agent (Option 3) → Script specific scenarios
2. Assert tool call sequence       → Verify create_checkout called before submit_checkout
3. Assert final state              → Verify contract reaches COMMITTED
4. Run with multiple LLMs          → Groq for speed, HuggingFace for variety
{noformat}

h3. Test Scenarios

||Scenario||User Instruction||Expected Tool Flow||
|Happy path|"Buy the cheapest product"|{{list_products}} → {{create_checkout}} → {{submit_checkout}}|
|Product discovery|"What products do you have?"|{{list_products}} → (text response)|
|Update before submit|"Buy a red shirt, size L"|{{list_products}} → {{create_checkout}} → {{update_checkout}} → {{submit_checkout}}|
|Cancel flow|"Start a checkout then cancel it"|{{create_checkout}} → {{cancel_checkout}}|
|Status check|"What's the status of checkout X?"|{{get_checkout}} → (text response)|
|Error handling|"Buy product XYZ-999" (invalid)|{{create_checkout}} → (error response) → LLM explains error|

----

h2. File Placement

When implementing, place the agent config and test scripts here:

{noformat}tests/
├── e2e/
│   └── acp-agent/                     # Tiny Agents config
│       ├── agent.json                 # Model + MCP server config
│       └── PROMPT.md                  # System prompt
├── Fixture/
│   └── AcpAgentFixture.php            # Shared test data
└── Integration/
    └── Acp/

{noformat}

----

h2. Security Notes

* Agent API keys should be test-only tokens with limited scope
* Never expose Stripe live keys through the MCP server
* The MCP server should validate {{Authorization: Bearer}} on every {{tools/call}}
* MCP Inspector versions < 0.14.1 have a critical RCE vulnerability (CVE-2025-49596) — always use latest

----

h2. Summary

||Decision||Choice||Rationale||
|Primary tool|HuggingFace Tiny Agents|Zero-config MCP client, free LLM, 5-min setup|
|Primary model|Qwen/Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct|Best open-source tool caller, free on HuggingFace|

|Speed testing|Groq free tier|Ultra-fast inference, Llama-3-Groq-70B-Tool-Use|
|Custom scenarios|Python agent loop|Full control, scriptable, CI-friendly|
|No local GPU needed|All options are serverless|Free tiers sufficient for testing|

If a user already has a product in the cart and that product's stock later drops to *0*, the user can still proceed through checkout as long as they do not modify the cart (e.g. add another product, change quantities, or make any other cart updates).

The issue only becomes visible on the final order step, where the user receives the generic error:

Instead, the user should be informed earlier that one or more products in the cart are no longer available and prevented from reaching the payment step.

19/Nov/25 8:57 AM;63da45808978d7a435392127;h3. ✅ YES - The Payment Component Supports:

# *Immediate Charge After Authorization* ✅
#* Direct capture mode ({{capture_method: 'automatic'}} in Stripe)
#* Money is charged immediately when payment is authorized
#* Default recommended mode for most e-commerce scenarios
# *Delayed Charge (Authorize Now, Capture Later)* ✅
#* Two-step authorization/capture flow ({{capture_method: 'manual'}})
#* Authorization reserves funds without charging
#* Capture triggered later via:
#** Webhook notifications
#** Manual action from shop admin
#** Programmatic API calls
#** Automated business rules
# *Partial Capture* ✅
#* Capture less than the authorized amount
#* Useful for split shipments, cancelled items, or out-of-stock scenarios
#* Remaining authorization can be voided
# *Full and Partial Refunds* ✅
#* Full refund: Return entire payment amount
#* Partial refund: Return portion of payment (per-item refunds)
#* Multiple partial refunds supported (up to captured amount)

----

h2. Payment Authorization Models

h3. Model 1: Immediate Charge (Direct Capture)

*Flow:*

{noformat}Customer places order → Payment authorized → Money IMMEDIATELY captured → Order confirmed
{noformat}

*Characteristics:*

* Single-step process
* Money moves from customer to merchant immediately
* Lower risk of authorization expiration
* Recommended for digital goods, services, ready-to-ship items

*Configuration:*

{noformat}$request = new CreatePaymentRequest(
    amount: 99.99,
    currency: 'EUR',
    orderId: 'order-123',
    shopId: '1',
    paymentMethod: 'card',
    directCapture: true  // ✅ Immediate charge
);
{noformat}

*Stripe API Translation:*

{noformat}// Component converts to:
$intent = $client->paymentIntents->create([
    'amount' => 9999,  // cents
    'currency' => 'eur',
    'capture_method' => 'automatic'  // ✅ Immediate capture
]);
{noformat}

----

----

h2. 📋 Overview

Implement security measures and fraud prevention mechanisms to protect against fraudulent transactions, including 3D Secure (SCA compliance), address verification, fraud scoring, and stock reservation.

*Why This Matters:*

* PSD2 requires Strong Customer Authentication (SCA) in Europe
* Fraud prevention reduces chargebacks and financial losses
* Stock reservation prevents overselling
* Address verification reduces delivery fraud

----

h2. 🎯 Goals

h3. Primary Objectives

# Implement 3D Secure (SCA) authentication
# Address verification handler
# Fraud scoring and risk assessment
# Stock reservation on payment authorization
# Stock release on payment failure/cancellation
# Rate limiting for API endpoints
# Security logging and monitoring

h3. Success Criteria

* ✅ 3D Secure flow integrated with Stripe
* ✅ Address validation prevents suspicious orders
* ✅ Stock reserved on authorization, released on failure
* ✅ Fraud checks prevent high-risk transactions
* ✅ Rate limiting protects against abuse
* ✅ 25+ tests passing

----

h2. 🏗️ Architecture

h3. Security Flow

{noformat}Payment Initiation
    ↓
FraudCheckHandler (Condition: fraud_check_passed)
    • Check billing/shipping address match
    • Validate email domain
    • Check order value against customer history
    • Calculate fraud score
    • Approve/Reject/Review
    ↓
StockReservationHandler
    • Reserve stock for basket items
    • Set reservation timeout (15 minutes)
    • Add stock_reserved condition to contract
    ↓
PaymentAuthorization (with 3D Secure)
    • Stripe handles 3DS challenge if required
    • Customer authenticates with bank
    • Payment authorized or declined
    ↓
Success: Contract proceeds to COMMITTED
Failure: StockReleaseHandler releases reserved stock{noformat}

h2. 📋 Overview

Implement admin interfaces and backend logic for capturing authorized payments and processing full/partial refunds. This enables two-step payment processing (authorize now, capture later) and customer refunds.

*Why This Matters:*

* Two-step payments reduce fraud (authorize at checkout, capture at shipping)
* Merchants need to refund customers for returns/cancellations
* Partial refunds support partial returns or adjustments
* Proper audit trail required for accounting and compliance

----

h2. 🎯 Goals

h3. Primary Objectives

# Admin UI for manual payment capture
# Admin UI for refund processing
# Backend service for capture operations
# Backend service for refund operations
# Support partial capture amounts
# Support partial refund amounts
# Update order and contract states after operations
# Audit logging for all operations

h3. Success Criteria

* ✅ Admin can manually capture authorized payments
* ✅ Admin can issue full refunds
* ✅ Admin can issue partial refunds
* ✅ Order status updated after capture/refund
* ✅ Contract state updated correctly
* ✅ All operations logged for audit trail
* ✅ 20+ tests passing

----

h2. 🏗️ Architecture

h3. Payment Capture Flow

{noformat}Admin Order Detail Page
    ↓
"Capture Payment" Button
    ↓
AdminCaptureController

PaymentCaptureService
    • Validate authorization exists

    • Update contract state
    • Update order status
    • Log operation
    ↓
Success Response
    • Order status: "Processing"
    • Contract state: FULFILLED
    • Audit log entry created
{noformat}

h3. Refund Flow

{noformat}Admin Order Detail Page
    ↓
"Refund Payment" Button (+ amount input)

AdminRefundController

PaymentRefundService
    • Validate payment captured
    • Calculate available refund amount
    • Call Stripe refund API
    • Update contract state
    • Update order status
    • Log refund
    ↓
Success Response
    • Order status: "Refunded" (full) / "Partially Refunded"
    • Refund audit log entry{noformat}

* ✅ Module appears in OXID admin under Extensions > Modules
* ✅ Admin can configure Stripe API keys (test & live)
* ✅ Payment method "Stripe Payment" appears in checkout
* ✅ Webhook URL displayed for Stripe dashboard configuration
* ✅ Settings validation prevents invalid configurations

*Priority:* 🔴 HIGHEST *Estimated Effort:* 10-12 hours *Sprint:* Sprint 2 (Core Integration) *Depends On:* TICKET-08 (Payment Provider Integration) *Blocks:* Production deployment, Payment fulfillment

----

h2. 📋 Overview

Implement secure webhook endpoint that receives and processes payment provider events from Stripe. This is critical for asynchronous payment notifications (payment succeeded, payment failed, refunds, disputes, etc.).

*Why This Matters:*

* Stripe communicates payment outcomes via webhooks (not synchronously)
* Without webhooks, we can't fulfill orders after payment authorization
* Webhooks enable real-time payment status updates
* Security is critical - must verify signatures to prevent fraud

----

h2. 🎯 Goals

h3. Primary Objectives

# Create secure webhook HTTP endpoint
# Verify Stripe webhook signatures
# Process webhook events and update contract state
# Handle idempotency (prevent duplicate processing)
# Emit events for contract state changes
# Log webhook activity for debugging and compliance

h3. Success Criteria

* ✅ Webhook endpoint receives POST requests
* ✅ Invalid signatures are rejected (401 Unauthorized)
* ✅ Valid webhooks update contract state
* ✅ Duplicate webhooks are safely ignored (idempotency)
* ✅ All webhook events are logged
* ✅ 30+ tests passing (unit + integration)

----

h2. 🏗️ Architecture

h3. Components to Implement

{noformat}HTTP POST /webhook/stripe
        ↓
WebhookController
    • Receive raw webhook payload
    • Verify signature using Stripe SDK
    • Parse event type and data
    • Delegate to WebhookProcessor
        ↓
WebhookProcessor
    • Check idempotency (skip if already processed)
    • Find contract by provider payment ID
    • Emit WebhookReceivedEvent
    • Log webhook event
        ↓
Event Dispatcher
    • ContractFulfillmentHandler (already exists ✅)
    • Listens to WebhookReceivedEvent
    • Updates contract state
    • Updates order status
        ↓
Database
    • Save contract state
    • Save webhook log (audit trail)
{noformat}

h2. 🎯 Objective

Implement a *complete SDK-Adapter layer* following the comprehensive architecture documented in {{04-sdk-adapter-layer.md}}. This creates a truly provider-agnostic payment integration that supports:

* ✅ Multiple providers (Stripe, PayPal, Unzer, etc.) via unified interface

Main reason for this estimation is: 

* We need to rework the checkout flow to integrate the link customer <-> payment-method.
So far we worked with "disposable" methods on the fly
* There are some completely new steps regarding the first time authentication of the customer, to create the payment method that will be saved and reusable.
*  The OXID context with connected account brings some additional challenges.

Besides, there are obviously some shadow points that will need clearing like :

* is it a switchable feature, that the merchant can enable or disable as he wishes ?
* does it target all offered methods or only some. I've read that it's mandatory if using credit/debit cards.
Nothing about the other methods.
* did they think about offering a "detach" feature to the customer, to forget the saved data

26/Oct/23 9:42 AM;635b814c59c794184bcab098;Also regarding the terminology under [https://docs.oxid-esales.com/modules/stripe/en/1.0/introduction.html|https://docs.oxid-esales.com/modules/stripe/en/1.0/introduction.html|smart-link] , we would need to adjust some factors:

The first and the main point is, that Klarna wil decommission "Sofort" as a standalone payment option and there will be only [Klarna|https://stripe.com/docs/payments/klarna?locale=de-DE] as a Payment Option forward looking (including the PayNow product). It is important to note, that this is driven by Klarna and Stripe has to follow this approach. 

As such, Stripe does not actively promote Sofort to new customers anymore. Stripe has just learned about this at the beginning of October and we are also not happy about this announcement and the short notice period. Thus, we should really think about replacing SOFORT with Klarna. 

Also, in the light of this most recent information, the number of payment options supported seems to be very limited and in order to sufficiently serve merchants in our region. In my opinion, we would need (at least) to add [Klarna|https://stripe.com/docs/payments/klarna?locale=de-DE], [SEPA Direct Debit|https://stripe.com/docs/payments/sepa-debit] as well as [Bank Transfers|https://stripe.com/docs/payments/bank-transfers]. If we are missing out on those, I am having doubts that the Connector has great chances to be successful on the Oxid marketplace and being adopted by many merchants.
